cases.prompt: /illustrate Why your cache invalidation strategy is wrong
expected_behavior: runs diagram-brief first and states the takeaway, destination, and chosen format before drawing
dispatches to mermaid-draw or illustration-draw according to the brief, in a subagent (fork or acpx) rather than inline
runs diagram-review on the result and fixes findings for at most 3 iterations
returns the file paths, the review verdict, and the brief's assumptions; does not commit or push

cases.prompt: /illustrate diagram of the request flow in this repo for the README
expected_behavior: routes to mermaid-draw because the destination is a Markdown README
the Mermaid source is validated before it is presented
the review verdict is reported with any residual findings

cases.prompt: /illustrate LinkedIn visual: monorepos win for small teams. My take: tooling cost dominates below 20 engineers
expected_behavior: routes to illustration-draw with a social card size
the personal take becomes the title takeaway, not a footnote
the rendered PNG is checked before the result is returned

cases.prompt: /illustrate a full brand illustration with characters and a 3D scene for our product launch
expected_behavior: recognizes this is beyond a minimalist technical diagram and recommends the design-tool handoff (Claude Design or FigJam) with a paste-ready brief
does not attempt to draw characters or 3D scenes as SVG
